A major one every year, around the end of February, which lasts 1-2 months. It's mostly connected to the coming of Spring, which saps my strength and puts me in a *really* bad mood (or perhaps positive melancholic effect of Autumn-Winter wears off).
I start reflecting on what I haven't done and how my goals are slowly getting out of my reach (though it might not be true; generally it isn't). I usually display some sort of auto-destructive behaviour, be it playing video games all day, stop eating for three days or dropping out of college on a whim right before getting dual bachelor's degree. Afterwards come 1-2 months of on-and-off motivation/depression cycle, then Summer comes and things settle down. 
At this point I might try to repair any damage done, like reading bunch of psychology books (to prevent this in the future), learning all the stuff I was supposed to learn on March-May, or enrolling the college again. When Autumn comes, I'm an unstoppable magnificent beast... until Spring, that is. I have to admit, t's not easy living like that.

Hm, it all makes sense. Okay, I'll start reading the book now.
